neighbours.label: the first half of a two-way split introduced by 'with': the token right after the first item ('with 12 [in] the old town and 18 by the harbour', 'with rows [on] the left and totals on the right')
fire: The class has 28 pupils, with 15 in the morning group and 13 in the afternoon.
Lay out the sheet with dates on the top row and names down the side.
The firm employs 90 people, with 60 in Leeds and 30 in Hull.
The chart shows the survey with ages on the horizontal axis and income on the vertical.
There are nine bedrooms, with five on the first floor and four in the attic.
Store the samples in a grid with controls in the first column and treated cells in the rest.
The league has 20 teams, with 12 in the north and 8 in the south.
The board is set up with pawns on the second rank and pieces behind them.
quiet: The class has 28 pupils, and they all study in the morning group.
Lay out the sheet with care before you write any names on it.
The firm employs 90 people and moved to Leeds in March.
The chart shows the survey answers sorted by the age of each person.
There are nine bedrooms, and the attic was converted last year.
Store the samples in a grid with a lid to keep out the dust.
The league has 20 teams, and the season starts in the north.
The board is set up with great care by the club's oldest member.

short: 'with X [in] A and Y in B'
notes: The + pole fires on 'On the one hand,' / 'For some,' - the opening of a two-part contrast - and this pole looks like the same distinction inside a 'with' clause. Probes: split 'with' clauses 0.57 and 0.62 (weaker forms 0.11-0.32); comitative 'with her brother on Tuesday' 0.02.
